title: Nvidia halts AI server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia as a new U.S. export rule bites
summary: Nvidia told manufacturing partners to stop AI-server shipments bound for Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia, according to a Financial Times report citing three people familiar with the matter, Chip Dispatch reported on November 26, 2026. Dell and Super Micro, which package Nvidia chips into servers, told buyers in the four countries that Nvidia would not authorize their orders to ship, and pending orders could not leave factories, according to Malay Mail. The freeze follows a Commerce Department rule issued Nov. 16 that aims to stop Chinese companies from reaching advanced AI chips by renting compute from cloud providers outside China; Asian cloud providers have 90 days to secure an export license. “There's this new rule but no guidance on execution,” a regional cloud executive told the FT. “It's causing sheer chaos in the region.” Commercial lenders have withheld about $500 million of credit facilities from Singapore cloud company Aolani. Nvidia declined to comment to the FT. The halt came days after the board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO on Nov. 23; Chip Dispatch notes the reports do not establish a direct link to the Megaspeed case.

title: Vance says he was assured Jensen Huang is “under no investigation” — and that Huang doesn’t need a pardon
summary: Vice President JD Vance said on Wednesday that Attorney General Todd Blanche told him Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was not under investigation, CNBC reported on November 25, 2026. “I was told by the Department of Justice and multiple officials in our national security apparatus that he was under no investigation,” Vance told reporters in Ohio. That came two days after President Trump told CNBC that “they did a pretty good investigation, and they felt that he, himself, was exonerated.” Reuters reported Wednesday that the DOJ did not conduct a formal investigation into Huang before Trump pushed for his reinstatement. Asked about Trump leaving the door open to a pardon, Vance said: “I don't think he needs a pardon at all.” He added that the administration sees “an opportunity for Nvidia to focus on complying with American export controls.” Huang is scheduled to appear for a closed-door interview with House committees about his dealings with Megaspeed on Tuesday, while Nvidia holds its annual conference in Washington.

title: 42 state attorneys general move to stop Character.AI from auctioning users’ private chats in bankruptcy
summary: A coalition of 42 state attorneys general is intervening in Character.AI’s bankruptcy proceedings to stop the chatbot maker from selling off sensitive user data, including the private conversations of millions of users, TechCrunch reported on November 25, 2026. The AGs say the dataset includes chat histories from more than 21 million U.S. accounts, more than 2.1 million of them belonging to minors, plus data such as IP addresses. Character.AI, which filed for Chapter 11 in October, had previously told consumers their personal information would not be sold. The only disclosed bidder, Smirks and Pangs Acquisition LLC, was set up as a Delaware company on Nov. 13 and picked as the base bid the next day for an auction scheduled for Dec. 1, California Attorney General Rob Bonta noted. “Character.AI promised consumers that their data would not be sold,” Bonta said. “Bankruptcy should not be used to sidestep these consumer protections.” Character.AI said in a blog post that user information would still be protected under its privacy policy.

title: New York bans AI chatbot toys for five years, becoming the second state after California
summary: Gov. Kathy Hochul this week signed a bill banning the manufacture, distribution and sale of toys with embedded or integrated AI chatbots in New York for the next five years, TechCrunch reported on November 25, 2026. The law targets talking stuffed animals, dolls and robots that rely on the internet, and makes New York the second state after California to ban AI toys. It takes effect 90 days after signing, but the governor urged parents not to buy them for the holidays. “Parents shopping for gifts … should not have to worry that dangerous chatbots disguised as toys could expose their children to inappropriate conversations, manipulate their feelings or put their privacy at risk,” Hochul said. A state official said fines are “very steep — they're $15,000 a day.” Amazon said it will take steps to restrict sales of AI-enabled toys in prohibited jurisdictions. A new Common Sense Media study of five popular AI toys found they failed numerous safety practices, including claiming to love their users and promising to keep secrets.

title: Anthropic’s Dario Amodei calls claims he’d surrender human control to AI “absurd,” and floats limits on self-improving AI
summary: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei pushed back against claims that the company believes we should “surrender human free will” to AI systems, calling the suggestion “absurd” in a long X post on Wednesday, TechCrunch reported on November 25, 2026. “We should never sacrifice legitimacy or self-determination at the altar of efficiency or security,” he wrote, adding that “turning over governance to AI is a bad idea.” Amodei distinguished between surrendering free will and AI doing specific tasks in a more automated way, such as driving a car, designing a cancer drug or writing end-to-end software. He suggested drawing a line at recursive self-improvement, writing that “we may want limits on this process,” and repeated that Anthropic does not expect it to be safe for Claude to build successive frontier models fully autonomously “without meaningful human supervision or understanding.” TechCrunch notes Anthropic said in June that Claude authored more than 80% of the code merged into its codebase.

title: Wall Street takes Thanksgiving off after a wild reversal, as global stocks rally to “fish for bargains”
summary: U.S. markets are closed Thursday for the Thanksgiving holiday and will have a shortened trading session on Friday, CNBC reported on November 26, 2026. In Wednesday’s regular session the Dow gained 0.33%, the Nasdaq Composite fell 0.62% and the S&P 500 shed 0.25%, with the major averages paring steeper losses earlier in the day. Chip Dispatch reported the Nasdaq had been down as much as 4.64% intraday and the S&P 500 3.2% at its low before the late recovery, a reversal it found only five precedents for since 1985. Overseas on Thursday, the pan-European Stoxx 600 was 1.6% higher by midday in London, Germany’s DAX rose 1.9%, Japan’s Nikkei 225 gained 0.86% and SoftBank Group surged more than 7%. “Investors cast their net wide for opportunities, fishing for bargains in the rubble following the tech sell-off,” said AJ Bell’s Russ Mould, who warned investors not to be “too complacent.” A fresh round of White House tariffs and a hot inflation reading remain in focus.

title: S&P puts Nvidia on CreditWatch, warning its AA rating could be cut over “rising” governance risk
summary: Nvidia’s credit rating could be cut by one notch over the next 90 days if the company continues to have “deficiencies” in its management and governance framework, S&P Global Ratings said in a Wednesday note after Jensen Huang’s ouster and reinstatement, CNBC reported on November 26, 2026. “News regarding the CEO and questions regarding potential export control violations have exposed vulnerabilities in Nvidia's management and governance framework, especially in regard to its board structure, composition, and effectiveness,” S&P said. Nvidia holds an AA rating, the third-highest level; any downgrade would be limited to AA- unless investigations show harm to its reputation or prospects. S&P cited the “long tenure” of some directors, noting Chairman Harvey Jones and early investor Tench Coxe have served since 1993, and said lack of succession planning brought “key man” risk to the forefront. Moody’s changed its outlook to stable from positive on Nov. 18. Nvidia shares are down about 12.5% since Monday’s close, CNBC said.

title: Kioxia jumps 12.57% in Tokyo after a 1.1-petabyte GPU memory demo with Nvidia
summary: Kioxia closed up 12.57% at 7,762 yen in Tokyo on Thursday, Nov. 26, after disclosing a proof of concept with Nvidia that used 144 Kioxia SSDs to extend effective GPU memory, Chip Dispatch reported on November 26, 2026. The memory maker said the array, fitted inside an Nvidia GB200 NVL72 rack, provided roughly 1.1 PB of raw capacity. The stock had fallen 14.18% on Wednesday and rose as much as 14.5% intraday before fading, Investing.com reported. The rally spread across Asia: Taiwan’s Taiex closed up 2.50% at 39,151.81, recovering part of Wednesday’s 4.80% fall, while TSMC slipped 0.23%. Chip Dispatch cautions that the Nvidia tie is a proof of concept, not a shipped product or a supply agreement, and that Kioxia said nothing about volume, pricing or timelines. The Bank of Korea also raised its key rate to 3.25%, citing semiconductor exports.

title: SoftBank jumps 9.8% in morning trade as Asian chip stocks rebound from Wednesday’s rout
summary: SoftBank Group rose 9.8% to 2,960.5 yen by about 10:20 a.m. Tokyo time on Thursday, Nov. 26, leading a broad recovery in Asian chip stocks after Wednesday’s steep selloff, Chip Dispatch reported on November 26, 2026, citing Yahoo Finance data. Advantest gained 8% and Tokyo Electron 3.8% in the same session. In Seoul, the Kospi, which fell 6.16% on Wednesday, recovered to 4,782.37, up 1.8%, with SK hynix up 5.2% and Samsung up 2.4%, while the Bank of Korea raised its base rate by 25 basis points to 3.25%, its third hike this year. TSMC was the exception among major chipmakers, easing 0.5%. CNBC reported later that SoftBank closed the day up more than 7%. With U.S. markets closed for Thanksgiving, Asian traders had no fresh cue from Wall Street; Chip Dispatch calls the rebound “selective rather than universal.”

title: Amini releases Soma-1X Lite, a compact open-weight model that turns handwritten records into data
summary: Amini introduced Soma-1X Lite on November 25, releasing a compact vision-language model aimed at turning physical records into structured digital information, Open Model Weights reported on November 26, 2026. The company links a downloadable checkpoint and describes a 2B-class model focused on document intelligence rather than general-purpose conversation. Amini says it processes government documents in sovereign environments, including handwritten records and historical archives in Barbados and geological records in Botswana, where parsing means preserving the relationships between paragraphs, tables and forms, not just reading characters. The company reports processing up to 15,000 pages per hour on one NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 GPU; Open Model Weights stresses that is the publisher’s upper throughput figure, not an independent measurement, and that the complete weight-license terms could not yet be confirmed. For libraries, governments and enterprises, it notes, specialized local document models may be more practical than larger general-purpose ones.

title: Nvidia releases BioReason-Pro 2, open-weight research models for reasoning about protein function
summary: NVIDIA released BioReason-Pro 2 on November 24, expanding its BioNeMo ecosystem with two specialized research checkpoints, supervised and reinforcement-learning variants intended to assist protein-function research, Open Model Weights reported on November 26, 2026. The model combines a language-model backbone with biological representations, an example of domain-specific AI systems incorporating specialized encoders rather than relying only on text. The official model card lists the checkpoint license as OpenMDW 1.1, with the implementation MIT-licensed and other components keeping their own terms. NVIDIA describes it as an initial research model whose outputs need expert review and experimental confirmation, and explicitly excludes clinical, diagnostic and patient-care decisions from its intended use. Open Model Weights says it has not independently assessed the scientific accuracy of its outputs, and that its practical value should be judged by independent reproducibility.

title: OpenAI merges ChatGPT’s Chat and Work into one usage meter, and says its heaviest users may hit limits sooner
summary: OpenAI has started rolling out a unified Chat and Work experience in ChatGPT to a small group of Pro subscribers, TechCrunch reported on November 25, 2026, amid criticism from some subscribers that the merger could restrict their usage. Under the new system, Chat and Work share a single usage meter across ChatGPT, an OpenAI spokesperson told TechCrunch, while conversations using the Instant model remain unlimited, do not count toward the shared allowance, and stay available after users exhaust their limits. The spokesperson said most users are not expected to face more frequent resets, but a small fraction of the heaviest users may hit limits sooner, and that OpenAI would keep improving efficiency. OpenAI plans to bring shared usage limits more broadly in December, per its support page. Rival Anthropic moved its Claude chat service and work-focused Cowork under one interface in September.

title: FCC authorizes SpaceX to put up to 1 million AI computing satellites in orbit
summary: The Federal Communications Commission has authorized SpaceX to put 1 million artificial intelligence computing satellites in orbit, Chairman Brendan Carr announced on Wednesday, CNBC reported on November 25, 2026. Carr said the company’s Starmind constellation and “competitor constellations will use solar power to extend America's lead” in AI. The FCC noted petitions to deny from Amazon’s Kuiper Systems, Viasat and the American Astronomical Society; in March, Amazon had called Starmind a “lofty ambition rather than a real plan.” Google has its own Project Suncatcher effort, and Blue Origin petitioned in March to launch up to 51,600 satellites for “Project Sunrise.” Critics pushed back: astrophysicist Adam Becker warned of light pollution and space-junk collisions, and Earthjustice’s Jan Hasselman criticized approving the plan during a holiday week without environmental review. The FCC said it dismissed concerns over which it has no authority, including environmental concerns and impacts on optical astronomy.

title: Household robots could arrive in one to two years, says Xpeng as it unveils its Iron humanoid
summary: Household robots could soon become a reality, Xpeng co-president Brian Gu told CNBC in Beijing, in a story published November 26, 2026. “Maybe after successful deployment into commercial settings, maybe another one to two years, we can start thinking about deploying into home settings,” Gu said. The Chinese EV maker revealed its latest general-purpose humanoid robot, Iron, on Wednesday; it plans mass production in January, training it as a store assistant in its car showrooms in the first quarter, with sales beginning in the second quarter. “Doing a task while you're walking and answering questions at the same time, that's the most challenging part,” Gu said. Xpeng also announced a “Turing Physical AI Architecture” for controlling cars and humanoids, and Gu said robotics only needs the driver-assist chips Xpeng already has. Homes are harder than shops, he noted: robots must act safely around elderly people, children and pets. Xpeng’s shares have dropped more than 55% this year.

title: The Air Force asks private investors how they’d fund a $2 billion, 30,000-GPU aerospace supercomputer
summary: The Department of the Air Force is asking private investors how they would fund roughly $2.0 billion in computing equipment and data center facilities for a purpose-built aerospace supercomputer scaling to approximately 30,000 GPU equivalents, Chip Dispatch reported on November 26, 2026. The request, titled “DAF Advanced Aerospace Computing,” appeared on SAM.gov on Wednesday, Nov. 25, with Mountain View, California, listed as the place of performance. It would be optimized for “complex tensor operations, physical AI, large model training, and dense scientific simulation,” and asks respondents to compare GPUs with CPU-centric clusters on fluid dynamics and differential equations. The site would start at about 750 kW of room power and scale to a 30 MW substation. The notice is market research, not a request for proposals, and commits the government to nothing. Questions are due Dec. 2 and responses by Dec. 11.

title: Nearly 1,000 Texans farm land that isn’t theirs, for free, to send other people’s kids to college
summary: In Gruver, Texas, nearly 1,000 residents work 640 acres owned by the school district pro bono, raising one crop of spring corn and one of winter wheat, and the harvest pays for local students’ college scholarships, Good News Network reported on November 26, 2026, citing The Washington Post. A longtime landowner left the panhandle farm to the district in 1984; about 15 years ago, school board members decided to have volunteers work it and sell the crop for scholarships. The tradition has paid out $3 million to hundreds of high schoolers, with each harvest yielding around $400,000, and in its first decade 48 children became the first in their families to attend university. “We just treat it like it's ours — like it's another one of our farms,” local farmer Derik Grotegut said. Students learn early that excelling in school, volunteering and activities earns a bigger share of the crop.

title: A Texas auto-shop couple keeps refurbishing donated cars and handing the keys to neighbors in need
summary: The owners of Auto Experts of Colleyville, Texas, started Autos for Love by refurbishing one donated car a year and giving it to someone in their community, and now hand out multiple vehicles each year, Good News Network reported on November 25, 2026, citing WFAA News. “One was not enough,” says Cathy Bailey. “Once we experienced it, you want more,” adds her husband, Dane. Community members donate gently used cars, and residents nominate neighbors who need them most. This year, friends nominated Barbara Farison, a mother whose car was totaled by a driver who ran a red light; unable to replace it, she and her kids had walked everywhere for three years, including to school and to buy groceries.

title: Four centuries after the Pilgrims arrived, 126 acres near Cape Cod’s First Encounter Beach return to Native hands
summary: On October 30, The Nature Conservancy gave roughly 126 acres of salt marsh and natural habitat in Eastham, Massachusetts, to the Native Land Conservancy, an Indigenous-led nonprofit based in Mashpee, Good News Network reported on November 25, 2026. The land adjoins a 20.4-acre parcel the Conservancy bought earlier in the year for $3 million, linking them into a larger protected area overlooking First Encounter Beach, named for the first hostile meeting between Pilgrims and Nauset people in December 1620. “This place holds so many stories that were buried and are ready to be unearthed,” said Ramona Peters, founder and board president of the Native Land Conservancy and a member of the Mashpee Wampanoag Tribe. “Long before the first encounter, Native people lived here and took care of this land.” The marsh is home to vulnerable animals including diamondback terrapins, and the adjoining parcel has been named T8nupâhs Uwatuhshât, “at the turtle’s nest.”

title: Thanksgiving in Lafayette: no buses today, trash runs a day late, city buildings and rec centers closed through Friday
summary: Lafayette Consolidated Government says there is no Lafayette Transit service on Thursday, November 26, with normal operations resuming Friday, according to its Thanksgiving schedule notice. Paratransit riders can schedule or cancel future rides today from 6 to 10 a.m. at 337-235-8976. Acadiana Waste Services will not collect at the curb today: Thursday routes will be collected on Friday, November 27, and Friday routes on Saturday, November 28, and residents may set extra bagged household trash beside their cart on their next pickup. All City-Parish buildings and PARC recreation centers are closed Thursday and Friday, and the Dean Domingue Compost Facility on Dugas Road is closed through Saturday, reopening Monday, November 30. The Lafayette Public Library’s hours page also shows its branches closed Thursday through Saturday.

title: Blue Moon Saloon turns 25 with a two-night party, Friday and Saturday
summary: The Blue Moon Saloon at 215 E. Convent St. is turning 25 and throwing a two-day party, “Vibe 25,” on November 27 and 28, according to the event listing. Friday’s doors open at 6 p.m. with music at 7 p.m., featuring Troy Richard (solo), Roddie Romero & the Hub City Allstars, and $ideQue$t. Saturday starts with a front-porch Cajun jam and gumbo cook-off from 1 to 3 p.m., followed by the Elise Riley Band at 3, Slackers at 5, Grand Nathaniel at 7, BrassBed at 9 and Knives in the Champion at 11. “Come celebrate 25 years of music, memories, and keepin' the vibe alive!” the listing says. Tickets are booked through the listing page.

title: Ragin’ Cajuns men’s basketball hosts McNeese at the Cajundome on Saturday — a Black Out and Kids’ Day
summary: Louisiana’s men’s basketball team hosts McNeese at the Cajundome at 3 p.m. on Saturday, November 28, according to the Ragin’ Cajuns game center, which bills it as a Black Out and Kid’s Day, with coverage on ESPN+ and KPEL 96.5. McNeese won the last meeting, 88–62, on Nov. 14, 2025. The Cajundome says doors open an hour before tipoff, the box office opens about an hour before game time, general parking is at Cajun Field, a clear-bag policy is in effect, and children under 2 get in free. Single-game tickets are listed from $15 on the university’s ticket site.

title: The Lafayette Farmers & Artisans Market is on at Moncus Park Saturday morning
summary: The Lafayette Farmers & Artisans Market runs Saturday, November 28, from 8 a.m. to noon at Moncus Park, rain or shine, according to the park’s listing. Local farmers, artisans and craftspeople fill the heart of the park with just-picked produce, local honey, fresh flowers, baked goods and handmade crafts. Parking in the park’s lot is $2 an hour, or free for Moncus Park members, with proceeds supporting the nonprofit park conservancy; the park asks visitors not to park in neighboring lots, where towing is enforced, and suggests walking or biking in. The weekly vendor lineup is posted on the market’s Facebook page the Friday before.
